reasons: The internal and public split is described but not enforced here.

terms.meaning: A table inside a spreadsheet file that stores repeated text once and refers to it by number.
A lowercase, dash-separated version of a name that is safe to use in web addresses and ids.
A fixed list of fields that are allowed to be shown publicly; anything else is hidden.
A phrase pattern that, when found in text, suggests a sales opportunity.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Setup and imports
sections.what: Sets the project root, the output folder, and the spreadsheet XML namespace needed to read the workbook.
sections.why: Reading the workbook requires the spreadsheet namespace; the other paths are fixed.
sections.watch_out: The root is worked out from this file's position, so moving the script breaks the paths.

sections.name: slug
sections.title: Make URL-safe ids
sections.what: Turns a company name into a lowercase id made of plain letters and digits, with dashes between words.
sections.why: Likely reason: ids need to be stable and safe to use in web addresses.
sections.watch_out: Two names that differ only in accents or punctuation can produce the same id.

sections.name: rows (part 1)
sections.title: Read client rows and identities
sections.what: Reads spreadsheet rows from row six onward, and holds the hand-typed table that gives each company its domain, sector, and aliases.
sections.why: Likely reason: the workbook is ambiguous, so identities are typed in directly, as the comments say.
sections.watch_out: Each company name in the spreadsheet must exactly match a name in the identity table.

sections.name: rows (part 2)
sections.title: Build account records
sections.what: Matches each spreadsheet company to its identity and builds an account record with aliases, a research key, an identity note, and internal relationship fields. Masdar's legal-entity alias shares its research with Masdar.
sections.why: Likely reason: the shared research key avoids researching the same group twice.
sections.watch_out: A company missing from the identity table stops the run. Osool has no domain by design, so it cannot be automatically researched.

sections.name: rows (part 3)
sections.title: Add transmission owners and write files
sections.what: Adds eight transmission system owners that are not in the client map, reads the solutions and trigger rules from the markdown, checks the totals, and writes the three JSON files.
sections.why: The header says these owners were added at the user's request, and the asserts confirm the expected totals.
sections.watch_out: The totals are hard-coded, so adding or removing a company needs the matching assert changed.

summary: Reads a client partner spreadsheet, a solutions document, and a hand-typed list of company identities, then writes three reference JSON files that feed the opportunity map.
purpose: Build the account, solution, and trigger-rule reference data for the opportunity map.
why: The docstring says relationship data stays on the server and that public responses are limited to an approved list. Company identities are typed by hand because the workbook is ambiguous.
how: Reads rows from the first sheet, starting at row 6. Matches each company to its hand-typed identity, which gives its domain, sector, and aliases. Adds a fixed list of transmission owners. Reads solution rows and signal rules from the markdown file. Checks the totals with asserts. Writes accounts.json, solutions.json, and trigger-rules.json.
inputs: A client map spreadsheet and a solutions markdown document, both in attached_assets, plus the identity table in the script.
outputs: Three JSON files in the opportunity-map data folder, and a console summary.
risks: The accounts file holds internal fields such as partners, managers, and active case counts. The docstring says public output is filtered, but that filtering is not in this file. A company missing from the identity table stops the run. The asserts hard-code expected totals, so any change to the source data needs the asserts updated.
debug: A KeyError on a company name means the identity table needs an entry for it. A failed assert shows which count is off. Confirm that internal fields are not returned by any public route.
